- Windows 7 wallpapers are about 100 KB each (wide and upright), so the app takes less space.
- Screen cover: five more charging looks (a neofetch-style system card, a clock, a flock of birds, a typed line, a warp of stars); the pictures of all the looks are on the main page.
- Windows 11 Settings: a sidebar of the groups, a search box and rounded rows.
- Windows menu: 50 small joke apps written by Pulse (answers, counters, fake scans, sequences of lines).
- Game Hub: the built-in and HTML games are one group cover at the end of the shelf; the shelf no longer rebuilds on every return from a game; the disc that flies into the console is smaller.
- Pulse's logo line is thinner.
- The launcher's music window opens as Windows Media Player in a Windows look, in a tall window.
- Quick search is off by default and see-through; the clock flyout closes itself instead of taking the launcher down.
- Sticky note widget: smaller, one cell.
- Files: contact, calendar, mail, GPX/KML, SQL, CSS and TSV open as text; MPEG and Ogg video play in the video player.
- This PC readings (processor, memory, temperature, battery) are sampled while the launcher is in front.
- Blended music player: the cover follows the page when it is pulled, the lyrics lie on the blurred cover, and an optional second row of buttons.
